summary.title: 500 Lines or Less: A Simple Web Server
summary.one_liner: You learn how HTTP requests and responses work at the socket level and how to build a small Python web server that serves static files, directory listings, and CGI scripts using a pluggable case-handler design.
keywords: build a web server in python
takeaways: HTTP is plain text: a method, URL, version, headers, and optional body in requests; version, headers, body, status code and phrase in responses.
Sockets, IP addresses and port numbers are the transport layer that HTTP runs over.
Python's BaseHTTPServer handles connection and parsing so you only write the do_GET logic.
Replacing if-chains in do_GET with a list of case objects (test/act) makes it easy to add directory listings and CGI support.
CGI runs external programs and sends their stdout back, but the chapter's implementation is explicitly insecure.
summary.summary: The chapter, part of the AOSA book's 500 Lines or Less collection, explains core web concepts: TCP/IP sockets, IP addresses and ports, HTTP request and response structure, status codes, statelessness and cookies, and URL parameters with encoding. It then builds a Python server step by step using BaseHTTPServer and the Requests library for testing. The server grows from a fixed page to dynamic pages, file serving with 404 errors, and a refactor into case classes that handle files, index.html, directory listings and CGI. The page text ends mid-section before the final refactor is complete.
